question: How does a run of the consumer repository prove to the service that it may submit captures?
context: Today the proof has two parts. The OIDC token of GitHub Actions says who calls. Two exact file hashes, of ci.yml and of app.yml, say which code ran. All of the cost comes from the file hashes: each edit of the 451 lines is a pin cutover of two repositories, with 34 to 41 minutes in which the runs of other pull requests fail (4 measured cases). Your note asks if API keys are simpler. A key replaces only the first part, and it makes the second part impossible. The options are in the order of work for the consumer, from the least to the most. No option adds a D1 write for a request, and no option gives a pull request from a fork a Visonaut check.

options.label: 1. Keep the OIDC token, and check no workflow file
options.explanation: The proof is the OIDC token alone. GitHub signs the repository, the commit, the run, and the job, and the service checks them as today. It compares no file hash. Lines 157 to 206 of oidc.ts, the two pins, the repository variable, and the pin runbook go away. The consumer needs no secret and no API key. This was option 1 of revision r2, and the option "Trust repository and successful jobs only" of the earlier decision A02.
options.consequences: Consumer: delete one line, then nothing for each kind of workflow edit, also for an update of Renovate. No secret to create, to store, or to replace. A new customer later needs 2 steps: install the GitHub App and add the workflow lines. The signed repository number binds each run to one project, with no key table. Gives up: a pull request of an account with push access can replace the Submit job, and then code of the pull request counts the changed pixels. It can also send the no-visual report for itself. What is left: the workflow edit is in the diff of that pull request, and the branch rule of ariakit/ariakit asks for 1 approval. The same 5 accounts can already pass false screenshots through the capture code (TRUST-03). The count of loose settings of D-AUTH-04 is then true only in a run that did not replace the Submit job. Does not work outside GitHub Actions: API keys can be added later as a second proof. The least to build: it deletes code in both repositories and needs one CLI release and one last pin cutover. Changes the earlier decisions A02 and D39 (a pinned file of Ariakit holds the list of the required capture jobs) and contract lines 218 to 230.

options.label: 2. Keep the OIDC token, and move the Submit job to a workflow file of the service repository
options.explanation: The Submit job becomes a reusable workflow in ariakit/visonaut, and app.yml calls it with one "uses" line. The service accepts a Submit only when the OIDC claim job_workflow_ref names that file on the branch main of ariakit/visonaut. The service accepts the no-visual report of the Plan job when ci.yml of the pull request is the same file as on main. No consumer file has a pin, and the consumer needs no secret.
options.consequences: Consumer: one refactor and one rule of 4 lines in renovate.json. The Submit job goes from 44 lines to 8, and the repository variable goes away. After that, no workflow edit and no update of Renovate needs a service change, and no failure window exists. Keeps what options 1 and 3 give up: a pull request cannot replace the Submit job, and it cannot send the no-visual report for itself. 2 accounts can change the Submit file in ariakit/visonaut. 5 accounts can push to ariakit/ariakit. Gives up: the service no longer checks the text of the capture steps and of the other CI jobs. Those steps already run pull request code (TRUST-03). A later customer calls the same file, so its capture jobs need the job names and the artifact names that the file expects. Cost for the service: the new workflow file, one CLI release, changes in the 7 files that compare a pin, and one last pin cutover. The package digest line of app.yml (PIPE-05) moves to the service file or goes away. Changes the earlier decisions A02 and D39 (the service file then holds the list of the required capture jobs) and contract lines 218 to 230. Not verified in these two repositories: one run before the cutover must confirm the claim for the branch main.

options.label: 3. Replace the OIDC token with an API key
options.explanation: A repository administrator creates a key on a settings page of the service. The page shows it one time. The consumer stores it as the repository secret VISONAUT_API_KEY and gives it to the CLI in 2 env lines. The service stores only a hash of the key, in one new D1 table, with own code and no library. The OIDC token and the file check go away. The GitHub App stays: it writes the check and reads the run (D-AUTH-02).
options.consequences: Consumer: create the key, add 1 secret and 2 lines, remove 3 lines. Then nothing for each workflow edit. A person must replace the key when someone with access leaves or when the key was in a log. A new customer later needs 4 steps. Gives: the proof that users of other products know (all 6 compared CI products offer a key), and a proof that can work outside GitHub Actions. Visonaut cannot use the second today, because the Submit job reads the capture artifacts of the run from GitHub. Gives up the same as option 1: a pull request can replace the Submit job. Gives up more: the key is the same in each run and has no end date. A workflow edit in a pull request can read it, and a copied key works from another computer until someone revokes it, also for the run of another pull request. For ariakit/ariakit this risk is not new: the same 5 accounts can read its 9 repository secrets in the same way today. The service loses the signed commit, run, and job, and must check them with GitHub. The most to build of options 1 to 3: a table, a settings page, a CLI change, and a new run check (estimate: 300 to 400 lines and their tests). With own code, a key check is 1 D1 read and 0 writes (local probe). The API key plugin of Better Auth writes 2 rows for each check, so it breaks the rule about D1 writes. Unkey is a second system to run. Changes A02, D39, and contract lines 218 to 230, as option 1.

options.label: 4. Keep today: the OIDC token and one exact file hash for each of two files
options.explanation: The service does not change. The contract row for A02 is corrected to say what production does. One procedure change needs no code: merge the consumer change with the admin bypass directly after the deployment.
options.consequences: Consumer: each edit of the 451 pinned lines costs a service pull request, a deployment, a variable change, and a failure window for the runs of other pull requests. An update of an action by Renovate cannot pass alone. Guarantee: only a file that the service maintainer reviewed can submit. With the bypass the window is minutes, and the consumer change merges without its own passed check. If the two files stay as they are, this option costs nothing. It does not scale to other customers: each workflow edit of each customer would need a deployment of the service.

rationale: Needed from you: is it enough that a workflow edit is visible in the diff of a pull request, which needs 1 approval? Or must a pull request not be able to replace the Submit job, the program that counts the changed pixels? If the diff is enough, option 1 is the smallest change, and it needs no secret. If not, option 2 fits: the consumer also does nothing for each later workflow edit. Select option 3 if you want the proof that users of other products know, or if a consumer must send captures from a system that is not GitHub Actions. No such consumer exists today, and keys can be added later as a second proof. Evidence that would change the recommendation of option 1: an account with push access that you do not trust with the result of the visual check, or a customer with a CI system other than GitHub Actions. Needed before a cutover to option 2: one run in ariakit/ariakit that shows the value of job_workflow_ref for the service file on the branch main.
